results.title: Ghana’s next oil bet: Can the Voltaian Basin end the country’s dependence on offshore fields?
results.content: The Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) says a rig could be on site by the end of the year. The big question is what happens to Ghana’s oil industry if the three main fields decline, and whether a basin drilled only once in 50 years can help. Ghana’s oil story has so far been written almost entirely at sea. Jubilee, TEN and Sankofa, the three fields that carry the country’s oil output, are all offshore. Now the national oil company wants to try something different: drilling on land. At the 2026 Petroleum Commission Local Content Conference, GNPC’s Chief Executive, Kwame Ntow Amoah, said the first piece of well equipment, the conductor casing, has already arrived at the drilling site. results.title: AGN Chair backs stronger inclusion of children in global climate negotiations
results.content: The Chair of the African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN), Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, has pledged the Group's support for efforts to strengthen the participation of children and young people in global climate change negotiations.

results.title: GH¢60,000 kidney treatment ordeal drives Pulima chief’s support for GMTF
results.content: The Paramount Chief of the Pulima and Gandawii Traditional Area, Kuoro Osman Deiwia Nankpa III, says a kidney condition that cost him more than GH¢60,000 to treat in 2008 has strengthened his support for the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF).

results.title: Non-interest banking is for everyone, not a religious tool – BoG Governor
results.content: The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr. Johnson Asiama, has dispelled misconceptions surrounding non-interest banking, clarifying that the financial model is a commercial, inclusive system designed to serve all demographics, regardless of religious or ethnic background.

results.title: Vegetable farmers urge gov’t to capture Anloga tomato factory in 2027 budget
results.content: Vegetable farmers in the Anloga District of the Volta Region have appealed to the government to include provision for a tomato processing factory in the 2027 national budget to address persistent post-harvest losses and improve their livelihoods.

results.title: GACL targets year-end start for Wa, Bolgatanga and Sunyani airport projects
results.content: The Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL) hopes to begin construction on airport projects in Wa, Bolgatanga and Sunyani before the end of 2026 to improve domestic connectivity and expand economic opportunities.

results.title: Dr Zanetor Rawlings calls for national sex offenders register to protect children
results.content: The Minister of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for the establishment of a national sex offenders register as part of efforts to strengthen child protection and curb sexual abuse against children.

results.title: Gender Ministry condemns death of five-year-old allegedly assaulted during parents’ dispute
results.content: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has condemned the death of a five-year-old pupil of Mim M/A Basic School in the Asunafo North Municipality of the Ahafo Region, following an alleged assault during a disagreement between her parents. The Ministry, in a statement issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, said it received news of the child’s death with shock and sorrow. According to reports cited by the Ministry, the disagreement between the parents escalated into violence, during which the child was allegedly assaulted and fell heavily to the ground. She died shortly afterwards, despite efforts to seek medical attention. “No child should lose their life in a place they ought to be safe,” the Ministry said as it extended condolences to the bereaved family, the school community and residents of Mim.

results.title: Only ‘cheap men’ will shield Obuasi SHTS headmaster – Bagbin warns politicians against interfering in assault case
results.content: Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has cautioned political leaders against shielding or interfering in the case involving the interdicted headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, who is facing sexual misconduct allegations.

results.content: The government is advancing plans to acquire new naval ships and aircraft for the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) as part of efforts to strengthen its operational readiness and military capabilities.

results.title: Military High Command briefs Defence Minister on the state of the Ghana Armed Forces
results.content: The Military High Command has briefed the Minister for Defence, Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, on the state of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), outlining ongoing efforts to improve personnel welfare, military infrastructure and operational capacity.

results.title: Anti-LGBTQ+ Bill: Parliament rescinds earlier passage; bill to return for further consideration
results.content: Parliament has rescinded its earlier decision to pass the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill 2025, following the discovery of inconsistencies between decisions taken by the House and the version of the legislation drafted after its third reading.

results.title: Ghana engages US civil rights lawyer Ben Crump over killings of nationals
results.content: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has approved the engagement of prominent US civil rights lawyer Ben Crump to assist Ghana in seeking justice for nationals killed in the United States in recent months. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, the Ministry said Ghana’s Permanent Mission in New York had been authorised to engage Mr Crump’s services at no cost to the Ghanaian taxpayer. “Approval has been granted to Ghana's Permanent Mission in New York to engage the services of celebrated US civil rights lawyer, Ben Crump, at no cost to the Ghanaian taxpayer, to assist Ghana in securing justice for all Ghanaians killed in the US in recent months,” the statement said. The Ministry said the decision reflected the government’s commitment to protecting the rights and dignity of Ghanaians living abroad.

results.title: Gov’t considers legal backing for GES Code of Conduct – Education Minister
results.content: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says the government is considering elevating the Ghana Education Service (GES) Code of Conduct into legislation to ensure teachers who engage in misconduct are dealt with decisively and in accordance with the law.

results.title: KNUST Researcher investigates how AI can improve brain scan analysis
results.content: How well can artificial intelligence developed using medical data from Europe and North America analyse brain scans from Ghanaian patients? This question took Ghanaian biomedical engineer Dr Prince Ebenezer Adjei to the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, where he worked with researchers to investigate how medical imaging AI tools perform on Ghanaian clinical scans.
